exam: 2022年6月 第2套 · 仔细阅读 P1
title: Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employ…

sents.en: Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employees, helping them to collaborate, share ideas and solve problems.
sents.cn: 社交媒体可以是员工强有力的沟通工具，帮助他们协作、分享想法并解决问题。

sents.en: Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes.
sents.cn: 研究表明，82%的员工认为社交媒体能改善工作关系，60%相信它能支持决策过程。

sents.en: These beliefs contribute to a majority of workers connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours.
sents.cn: 这些看法使得多数员工在社交媒体上与同事建立联系，即便是在工作时间。

sents.en: Employers typically worry that social media is a productivity killer; more than half of U.
sents.cn: 雇主通常担心社交媒体是生产力的杀手；

sents.en: S. employers reportedly block access to social media at work.
sents.cn: 据报道，超过半数的美国雇主在上班时屏蔽对社交媒体的访问。

sents.en: In my research with 277 employees of a healthcare organization I found these concerns to be misguided.
sents.cn: 在我对一家医疗机构277名员工的研究中，我发现这些担忧是被误导的。

sents.en: Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention.
sents.cn: 社交媒体对生产力的削弱，远不及它对员工留任的摧毁。

sents.en: In the first part of the study I surveyed the employees about why and how they used platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn.
sents.cn: 在研究的第一部分，我调查了员工为何以及如何使用Facebook、Twitter或LinkedIn等平台。

sents.en: Respondents were then asked about their work behaviors, including whether they felt motivated in their jobs and showed initiative at work.
sents.cn: 随后受访者被问及自己的工作行为，包括是否感到有工作动力、是否表现出主动性。

sents.en: I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas.
sents.cn: 我发现，通过社交媒体博客与同事进行在线社交互动的员工往往更有动力，也更能想出创新点子。

sents.en: But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative.
sents.cn: 但当员工与组织之外的人互动时，他们的动力和主动性都较低。

sents.en: In the second part of the study I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media.
sents.cn: 在研究的第二部分，我发现76%在工作中使用社交媒体的员工，对他们在社交媒体上发现的其他组织产生了兴趣。

sents.en: When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections.
sents.cn: 当我考察受访者如何表达对新的职业和雇主持开放态度时，我发现他们参与了一些关键活动，包括研究新组织、建立新的工作联系。

sents.en: These findings present a dilemma for managers: employees using social media at work are more engaged and more productive, but they are also more likely to leave your company.
sents.cn: 这些发现给管理者出了一道难题：在工作中使用社交媒体的员工更投入、更高效，但他们也更可能离开你的公司。

sents.en: Managers should implement solutions that neutralize the retention risk caused by social media.
sents.cn: 管理者应采取措施，消除社交媒体造成的留任风险。

sents.en: They can create social media groups in which employees will be more likely to collaborate and less likely to share withdrawal intentions or discussions about external job opportunities.
sents.cn: 他们可以创建社交媒体群组，让员工更可能协作，更不可能分享离职意向或讨论外部工作机会。

sents.en: Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories.
sents.cn: 管理者也可以利用社交媒体，通过认可员工的成就、让员工成功故事被看见，来直接降低离职意向。
